note: Agents build the gears into a real constant-mesh parallel-shaft gearbox (housing plates + 2 shafts + 4 library bearings + bored gears), judged by the full merge gates (gear_mesh + bore_fit + mass). DERIVE = each gear agent computes its tooth count; RESOLVE = handed its literal reconciled count (the RFC 11.1 resolve step). Two regimes: shared-CONSTANT (clean-integer teeth, easy) and GRID shared-RECONCILIATION (half-integer ideal split, must sum to 48). Full write-up: tests/MULTI_AGENT_EVAL.md.
finding: A shared CONSTANT each agent applies locally is easy (all conditions 48/48 across both sizes). A shared RECONCILIATION across agents is hard: DERIVE fails for everyone (partition 0/6 by independent rounding; single's per-gear cold calls also fail to reconcile, 0/6 at 12 gears), and the RESOLVE step fixes all of it (6/6) by handing each agent its literal reconciled tooth count -- tchainu -> tchainu_r on a real mechanism.
